title: Connect Drive to your computer
subtitle: With WebDAV, Drive opens like a folder in Finder, Windows Explorer or rclone. Drag and drop files and edit them in place; changes show up for everyone right away.

address.title: Connection details
address.serverHint: Your spaces appear as top-level folders under this address.
address.userHint: Your e-mail address. The server ignores the user name; the token in the password identifies you.
address.passwordValue: Your personal API token (starts with mhp_)
address.passwordHint: Reading needs the "Read and search" scope; writing and deleting files needs "Write Drive". You can limit the token to the spaces you choose.
address.tokensOff: Personal tokens are turned off in your organization. Ask an admin to turn them on under Administration › MCP and API to use WebDAV.

mac.step1: In Finder choose Go › Connect to Server (⌘K).
mac.step2: Paste the server address and click Connect.
mac.step3: Choose "Registered User", enter your e-mail as the name and your token as the password. You can save it in the keychain.
mac.note: Finder's ._ and .DS_Store files are not written to Drive.

windows.step1: In File Explorer choose This PC › Map network drive.
windows.step2: Enter the server address as the folder and tick "Connect using different credentials".
windows.step3: Enter your e-mail as the user name and your token as the password. You can also connect from the command line:
windows.noteHttps: Windows sends the password over https only; the address must start with https.
windows.noteSize: By default the Windows WebDAV client refuses files over 50 MB. Raise the limit in the registry (WebClient › FileSizeLimitInBytes) or use rclone for large files.

linux.step1: In Files (GNOME) go to Other Locations and enter the address below under Connect to Server.
linux.step2: Enter your e-mail as the user name and your token as the password. In KDE Dolphin use the same address with webdavs://.

notes.title: Good to know
notes.spaces: Every space you belong to is a top-level folder, your personal space among them.
notes.types: Only folders and files show up over WebDAV. Pages, boards and drawings stay in the web app.
notes.versions: Saving an existing file adds a new version; older versions stay in the Versions panel in Drive.
notes.trash: Files and folders you delete go to the trash and can be restored from there.
notes.rights: You only see files you have access to, and cannot write where you are a viewer.
